Use semantic or otherwise documented versioning consistently.

Plan maintainer succession and avoid single-person release authority.

Document the shared-responsibility boundary for every managed service and control.

Use workload and human identities with least privilege and strong authentication.
Inventory regions, zones, endpoints, public exposure, service policies, keys, and quotas.
Encrypt and control data according to sensitivity and residency requirements.

Include provider incidents and control changes in internal risk and postmortem processes.

Scan final images and monitor them after release.

Define resource requests, limits, priorities, disruption, and eviction behavior.
Use workload identities rather than shared node or cluster credentials.
Keep secrets out of images and ordinary environment output.
Restrict network communication to declared flows.

Define timeout, memory, payload, temporary storage, connection, and concurrency limits.

Configure dead-letter, failure destination, replay, and reconciliation.
